entry.name: SharpaDex v1.0
entry.title: SharpaDex v1.0: Large-Scale Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Demonstrations
entry.summary: Teleoperated bimanual demonstrations on Sharpa's North robot with two 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hands: 28,993 episodes of 59 tabletop tasks, with a 6-axis force/torque reading plus deformation and raw tactile video from each of the 10 fingertip sensors at 30 Hz.
entry.hand: Sharpa Wave (22 DoF) x 2 on Sharpa North (two 7-DoF arms + 7 torso/motor joints)

sensor.note: Five fingertip sensors per hand (Sharpa Wave built-in), no palm. Per frame: observation.tactile (60,) float32 = (left, right) x (thumb, index, middle, ring, little) x (fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz), unit not stated; observation.images.tactile_deform, one 480x1200 H.264 video tiling 10 deformation maps of 240x240 (2 rows x 5); observation.images.tactile_raw, one 480x1600 H.264 video tiling 10 raw sensor-camera images of 320x240. Per-episode fz maxima are 5.7-49.8 and torque magnitudes stay below 0.9 in the 23 episodes checked.
sensor.model: Sharpa Wave fingertip tactile sensor (Dynamic Tactile Array)
sensor.range: 0-30 N detection, 50 N maximum load (maker spec, Sharpa Wave W01 page)

scale.text: 28,993 episodes, 59 tasks, 32,396,172 frames @30 fps (~300 h), 495 collection seasons from 11 stations, Mar-Jul 2026; every season is released twice (LeRobot v3.0 and v2.1)

entry.access: Hugging Face Sharpa-Robotics/SharpaDex-v1.0, ungated, ~7.7 TB (LeRobot v3.0 and v2.1 copies of every season), one LeRobot root per task/season folder; single seasons or v2.1 episode files can be fetched alone.
caveats: Fingertips only (10 sensors); no palm or phalanx touch.
Tactile units are not stated: observation.tactile is called a 'force/torque signal' with fx..tz names. The tile order inside the two tactile videos is not documented.
The card names neither the robot nor the hand ('two 7-DoF arms, two 22-DoF dexterous hands'); robot_type is 'robot' in all 495 seasons.
observation.state.tcp force/torque slots and the 7 torso joint torques are 0 in every episode; TCP units and rotation convention are not documented (rotation_type null).
v3.0 and v2.1 are two exports of the same 28,993 episodes; count them once.
Released as 495 separate LeRobot roots (task/season), not one root; the card recommends splitting by season.
The raw tactile video (480x1600) is the largest stream: ~45-140 MB per 15-50 s episode in the v2.1 export.

Some seasons also appear in FTP-1-Dataset's sharpa/ archive (catalog entry ftp1_sharpa, MIT per ModelScope): 15 of 92 sampled FTP-1 sessions carry the same station and session timestamp as SharpaDex seasons of place_pens_in_holder, insert_plug_into_socket and place_books_on_shelf (POC22007 and POC22018, 2026-03-16 to 03-20). FTP-1 holds more episodes per shared session (52 vs 37 in one checked session) and only 3 fingertip deformation maps per hand. Sharpa's Robotic Origami Challenge and RoCo releases come from the same stations but share no season with SharpaDex.

tracking.system: Sharpa Wave hand joint states, 22 per hand
tracking.note: observation.state / action = 65-D: left arm 7, left hand 22, right arm 7, right hand 22, torso/motor 7; observation.state.joint_torque (65, torso dims 0)

tracking.system: arm joint encoders (2 x 7) and observed / commanded TCP poses (2 x 6)

tracking.note: card: 'human teleoperation of a real bimanual robotic system'; teleoperation device not named

other: tactile deformation video and raw tactile video (10 fingertips tiled in one frame each)
language: structured global task (task, instruction, scene, success) + 217,642 frame-aligned subtask segments with 45 skill labels

unconfirmed: Robot name 'Sharpa North' is inferred: annotations.jsonl anno_path reads '/mnt/netdata/Team/Academic/Data/North/SharpaOpenData/...', and the RoCo challenge page (co-organized by Sharpa) calls the same 65-D platform 'Sharpa North: A dexterous hand-based mobile manipulator with two robotic arms and 22-DoF hands'. The SharpaDex card names neither robot nor hand.
Hand identified as Sharpa Wave from the maker, 22 joints per hand, and the sensor output matching the Wave W01 spec (240x240 tactile resolution, 6-dimensional force/torque Fx..Mz).

Tactile tiles: 480x1200 = 2 x 5 tiles of 240x240 and 480x1600 = 2 x 5 tiles of 320x240, by division (T-Rex releases the same sensor as separate 240x240 deform and 320x240 raw streams). Row 0 = left hand, row 1 = right hand, columns thumb..little: read from one deformation frame (clean_plate_with_eraser ep 0, frame 701), where blobs appear exactly on the tiles whose fingertip |F| exceeds 2.

Unit of observation.tactile not stated; magnitudes look like N and N m (per-episode fz maxima 5.7-49.8, torques < 0.9, rest ~0, in 23 episodes). The clean_plate_with_eraser season's stats.json has fz max 76.3, above the W01 spec's 50 N maximum load, so N is not confirmed.
Principle set to optical from the card's wording ('raw tactile camera layout'); Sharpa's pages call the sensor a Dynamic Tactile Array without naming the principle.

hours=300.0: 32,396,172 frames / 30 fps = 299.96 h; episode and frame totals summed from all 495 v3.0 info.json files (v2.1 episodes.jsonl gives the same); per-task counts match the card's table for all 59 tasks.
Episode lengths 10.0-323.8 s (median 28.8 s); 24,453 of 28,993 are 10-60 s (from v2.1 episodes.jsonl).

Stations: season names carry a station id (POC22002 ... POC22065, 11 ids) and a start time from 2026-03-10 to 2026-07-07; read as collection stations and dates (not documented). Episodes per station: POC22027 7,758, POC22018 6,696, POC22048 6,594, POC22007 2,335, POC22032 1,663, POC22050 1,037, POC22054 994, POC22061 886, POC22065 585, POC22002 423, POC22021 22.
Head cameras are two streams (head_left, head_right); whether they form a calibrated stereo pair is not stated. Camera models not stated.
All 495 v3.0 info.json files list H.264 for the 6 video streams; the card says 'Codec may differ between exports'. Probed: the v3.0 and v2.1 tactile_deform files of one season are H.264 (avc1).
Annotation tags carry 'score' (S or B in the files read) and 'SOP' (V1.0 / V1.1 / empty); their meaning is not documented.
Torso/motor joints (state dims 58-64) are constant in some episodes and move by up to ~0.6 rad in others.
Chinese name: a third-party article (VCA创投社, 2026-09-02) writes 'Sharpa（大裂谷）' [Sharpa (Great Rift Valley)]; no official Sharpa page with a Chinese name was found, so zh is omitted.

FTP-1 overlap derived from session names, not stated by either release: SharpaDex place_pens_in_holder/season_POC22007_2026_03_16_15_28_42_train = FTP-1 sharpa/pick_place_pen_season_POC22007_2026_03_16_15_28_42_train.zarr; in that session all 37 SharpaDex episode lengths occur in the same order among FTP-1's 52 episodes (one session checked at episode level). 15 matches come from 92 FTP-1 sessions sampled by tar-header range reads; the full FTP-1 session list was not indexed, so the total overlap is not known. FTP-1 sessions are dated 2026-01-15 to 03-21; SharpaDex's earliest season is 2026-03-10.

sample.reason: Public, ungated Hugging Face release under CC BY-NC 4.0, which allows non-commercial redistribution with attribution. v2.1 stores one parquet and six mp4 files per episode, so single episodes can be fetched. Label the collection 'CC BY-NC 4.0'.

episodes.scene: tabletop, plug and socket; station POC22007
episodes.why: Insert, one hand. Right thumb and index in contact 14.0 / 14.6 s continuous (peaks 26.3 / 40.2). Grade S.

episodes.scene: tabletop, 500 ml PET bottle; station POC22048
episodes.why: Twist, two hands. Left hand holds the bottle with 5 fingertips (thumb-ring 24-29 s continuous, peaks 7-25; little 8.9 s); right thumb, index and middle turn the cap (8.7-11.5 s in total, peaks 13-19). 8 of 10 fingertips in contact.

episodes.scene: tabletop, marked plate and blackboard eraser; station POC22027
episodes.why: Wipe with a tool, two hands. Left 5 fingertips hold the plate 8.9-17.4 s (peaks 12-34); right thumb, index and middle hold the eraser 4.1-7.2 s continuous (peaks 21-37). Same season as the card's metadata example.
Deformable object, two hands. Thumb and index of both hands pinch the towel 6.4-6.6 s continuous (right 12 s in total); peaks 6-12, the lowest forces among the picks.

episodes.scene: tabletop, hammer and wooden peg bench; station POC22048
episodes.why: Tool use with impacts, one hand. All 5 right fingertips grip the hammer (thumb 20.0 s, index 8.9, middle 10.4, ring 10.1, little 8.3 s; peaks 10-21). Annotation grade B with 15 segments and no skill labels.

episodes.scene: tabletop, spoon and two cups with salt; station POC22048
episodes.why: Spoon scooping, one hand. Right thumb, index and middle hold the spoon 13.3-16.3 s (peaks 8-15).

episodes.scene: tabletop, card stack and tray; station POC22018
episodes.why: Fine bimanual handling: left hand holds the deck (thumb 3.6 s, peak 2.6), right thumb, index and middle extract and flip 5 cards (5.7-7.1 s continuous; thumb 24.2 s and index 18.5 s in total; peaks 15-30). 26 annotated segments.
Pick and place, one hand. Right thumb, middle and ring wrap the ball 3.5-4.4 s (peaks 13.5-28.5); index under 1 s.

sample.fetch_estimate: ~1.3 GB: all 6 v2.1 videos of the 8 episodes total 1,283 MB (tree API sizes: 105, 221, 115, 229, 195, 141, 219, 58 MB), of which tactile_raw is 713 MB; parquets 1-3 MB each. Already local: the 8 parquets (scan). Re-hosted media: tactile_raw (29-140 MB per episode at 480x1600) must be re-encoded smaller to stay under ~30 MB per episode. Episode JSON: 60 values x 30 Hz x <=49 s ~= 88k numbers, under 2 MB.
sample.rules_applied: 59 tasks, so 8 were taken, spanning insert (plug), twist (bottle cap), wipe with a tool (eraser), deformable folding (towel), tool impacts (hammer), scooping (spoon), card dealing and pick-and-place (ball); one- and two-handed tasks; 4 collection stations (POC22007, POC22048, POC22027, POC22018) stand in for scenes. Candidates: random v2.1 episodes of 10-50 s from seasons on different stations, 22 scanned. Contact = fingertip |F| above the episode's starting median + 1.0 (release units) for at least 1 s continuous; every pick has 2-8 fingertips in contact for 3.5 s or more, no NaN, timestamps at exactly 1/30 s. All picks are 15-49 s, so no window is cut.
